c.tagline: Powder-white sands, dive-worthy reefs, and Bohol's laid-back island soul

taxi.color: n/a — no metered taxis; tricycles and habal-habal only
taxi.fare: Tricycle short ride: ₱20-50 per person; habal-habal or multicab to Tagbilaran (~12km): ₱100-150
taxi.fareNote: Fares are negotiated/flat-rate; resorts also arrange private van transfers for tours and the airport

emergency.police: 911 (national emergency hotline) or Panglao Municipal Police Station
emergency.medical: Governor Celestino Gallares Memorial Hospital and Ramiro Community Hospital in Tagbilaran City (~20km) are the main referral hospitals
emergency.note: For diving injuries, the nearest hyperbaric chamber is in Cebu City — dive operators carry evacuation protocols. Travel insurance with medevac coverage is recommended.

hood_desc: Panglao's busiest tourist strip — a lively stretch of dive shops, beachfront restaurants, massage stalls, and bars right on the white sand, with the widest range of budget-to-mid lodging.
A quieter beach on the island's west side, known for calm, shallow snorkeling reefs and a mellower, less commercial vibe than Alona.
A relaxed stretch of coast anchored by upscale beach resorts and calm swimming waters, popular with couples and families seeking a quieter alternative to Alona.
The municipal center of Panglao, home to the historic Spanish-era church and watchtower, the public market, and everyday local life away from the beach crowds.
A long, wide stretch of white sand favored by resort guests for its calm waters and gentle slope — quieter and more spread out than Alona Beach.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; island tap water is not potable.

transit.pay: Cash only, fare negotiated or flat-rate up front
transit.map: n/a — no fixed routes; hail tricycles on the street or arrange through your resort
transit.note: Resorts commonly arrange private van transfers for island tours and the airport; renting a scooter is common for independent travelers.

bus: Buses/vans connect Tagbilaran to other Bohol towns and the Chocolate Hills
ferry: OceanJet fastcraft from Cebu Pier 1 to Tagbilaran Pier

airport.name: Bohol-Panglao International Airport
airport.note: ~2-7 km from most Panglao resorts (5-15 minutes). Resort shuttle, tricycle, or private van transfer; no metered taxis.

transit.m: Southwest shuttle van to Alona Beach (about 20 min)

tip.s: Tipping is not mandatory but increasingly common at resorts and restaurants — 10% is appreciated where no service charge is included
tip.r: Dive guides, boat crews, and tricycle/habal-habal drivers appreciate a small tip (₱50-150) for good service

food.desc: Visayan raw fish cured in coconut vinegar and calamansi with ginger, red onion and chilli; on Panglao it is usually tuna or wahoo.

places.name: Bohol Bee Farm

food.name: Lechon Boholano

places.name: Jose Panglao

landmarks: Alona Beach
Panglao's lively signature beach, a kilometer of white sand and turquoise shallows lined with dive shops, seafood grills and island-hopping bangkas.
Balicasag Island
A marine sanctuary ringed by coral walls where snorkelers drift with sea turtles and swirling jackfish, the highlight of every Panglao island-hopping tour.
Hinagdanan Cave
A limestone cavern lit by natural skylights, where stalactites drip above an eerily glowing underground lagoon that visitors may swim in.
Virgin Island (Pontod Sandbar)
A crescent sandbar rising from shallow turquoise water at low tide, a barefoot paradise of drifting sand and fresh sea-urchin snacks.
St. Augustine Church (Panglao Church)
A weathered 18th-century coral-stone church with a five-story watchtower, one of the tallest of its kind in the Philippines.
Our Lady of the Assumption Church (Dauis)
A graceful seaside church famous for the miraculous freshwater well at its altar's foot, mere meters from the salty sea.
Dumaluan Beach
A long, tranquil stretch of powdery white sand on Panglao's south shore, quieter than Alona and beloved for its shallow swimming and sunrise strolls.
Napaling Point
A dramatic reef drop-off on Panglao's north coast where freedivers plunge into swirling million-strong sardine balls just meters from the cliffside.
Chocolate Hills
Bohol's surreal signature landscape, more than a thousand grassy cone hills that turn cocoa-brown in the dry season, an essential day trip from Panglao.
Philippine Tarsier Sanctuary (Corella)
A forest reserve on nearby Bohol protecting the saucer-eyed Philippine tarsier, one of the world's smallest primates, seen dozing on quiet jungle trails.

train.note: There is no railway on Bohol or Panglao. Arrive by air into Bohol-Panglao International Airport, which opened in 2018 and sits on the island itself, or by ferry to Tagbilaran and across the causeway.

bus.note: No international coaches. Panglao is joined to Bohol by two causeways, and local buses, jeepneys and vans link Alona Beach with Tagbilaran in about 40 minutes; Ceres Liner covers the wider Bohol network from the Dao terminal in Tagbilaran, including the Chocolate Hills and Anda. Tricycles handle short hops on Panglao.

intl.to: Cebu City (Philippines) - fast craft from Tagbilaran, ~2 hr

ferry.note: There are no international sailings. The Cebu crossing from Tagbilaran port, about 20 minutes from Panglao, is one of the busiest routes in the Philippines with several OceanJet departures a day taking around two hours - book online in high season. Sailings are suspended when a typhoon signal is raised between roughly June and November. Boats to Balicasag and Virgin Island from Alona Beach are dive and day-trip charters.

half.name: Loboc River
half.blurb: A jungle river cruise past floating restaurants, with a dusk firefly-watching spot nearby, is about forty-five minutes away.

half.name: Baclayon Church
half.blurb: One of the Philippines' oldest coral-stone churches sits roughly thirty minutes from Panglao.

full.name: Danao Adventure Park
full.blurb: A highland zipline and canyon-swing park in Bohol's mountainous interior lies about two hours from Panglao.

full.name: Anda
full.blurb: A quieter stretch of white-sand coast on Bohol's east side with limestone caves and cenotes is about two hours away.

notes.walk: Alona Beach's main strip is walkable and packed with restaurants, dive shops, and bars, but Panglao island overall is spread out — reaching Doljo, Momo Beach, or the Bee Farm requires a tricycle, habal-habal, or rented scooter.
notes.card: Larger resorts and restaurants along Alona Beach accept cards, but tricycles, small eateries, and dive shops are often cash-only. ATMs are available around Alona Beach and in Tagbilaran City.
notes.safety: Very safe for solo travelers, including women — Panglao is a well-established, resort-driven tourist destination with a strong dive and hospitality community. Petty theft (unattended valuables on the beach or in unlocked rooms) is the main risk; violent crime against tourists is rare.
notes.religion: Roman Catholic 78.8%; Islam 6.4%; Evangelical 4.8%; Protestant 2.8%; Iglesia ni Cristo 2.6%; Other 4.6%
notes.net: Good coverage across Panglao from both national carriers. Most resorts and restaurants along Alona Beach offer free wifi; speeds vary and can slow during peak season. $2-6. Free wifi common at resorts and restaurants along Alona Beach. Prepaid tourist SIMs widely available.
notes.transit: No formal public transit system exists on Panglao
notes.transport: Fly into Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG), with direct flights from Manila and Cebu on Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific, and AirAsia. None — no rail service in the region. Buses/vans connect Tagbilaran to other Bohol towns and the Chocolate Hills; no direct bus service from Manila. OceanJet fastcraft from Cebu Pier 1 to Tagbilaran Pier, about 2 hours, multiple daily departures, then a 20-30 minute tricycle or van to Panglao. Rental cars and vans available in Tagbilaran; most visitors rely on resort transfers, habal-habal, or a rented scooter.
